# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 83 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | Coptic

---

## Saying 83

Jesus said: "The images are manifest to the human being, but the light within them is hidden in the image of the light of the Father. He will become manifest, and his image will be hidden by his light."

---

**Council Notes:**

- One of the most philosophically dense sayings in Thomas. The image-light dialectic:
  1. Images (visible forms) are apparent to humans.
  2. But the light *within* the images is hidden — it lies concealed in the image of the Father's light.
  3. When the Father is finally revealed, his image will be hidden *by his own light* — paradoxically, divine revelation conceals the form through excess of light.
- This is the Thomasine version of apophatic theology: the Father transcends any image of himself.
- "He will become manifest" — the Father as the subject; his revelation paradoxically conceals his image.
- All three agents agree substantially; SOPHIA follows EMET's more literal structure.
